subject: Performance support launch for Ethan Park — manager checklist
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Support plan for Ethan Park — need template + legal sign-off

Hi Jasmine,

Following up from last week's skip-level, I'd like to start a formal performance support path for Ethan Park (Eng, IC). Over the last two quarters we've documented repeated missed delivery dates, gaps on code review quality, and three Jira incidents where he missed on-call handoff procedure. I want to be careful about process here — manager-first approach, documented expectations, a measurable timeline, and legal/HR sign-off before we present anything.

Can you share the current support-plan template you prefer we use and any legal/pre-notice language we should avoid? Also:
- Recommended measurable goals for a 60-day window for a mid-level backend engineer
- Evidence log template for tracking follow-ups
- Standard manager script for the kickoff meeting

I can provide prior feedback notes and an evidence spreadsheet; attaching the quick summary.

Attachments: ethan_performance_summary.pdf (stub)

Thanks,
Karthik
Engineering Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Support plan for Ethan Park — need template + legal sign-off

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the summary and for pulling the evidence together. I attached our Performance Support Template (v1) and the manager checklist PDF — both are the starting point we use across engineering. High-level next steps I recommend:
1) Draft the specific, time-bound outcomes (I can help word them) — 60-day window with weekly checkpoints.
2) Share the draft with Legal for a quick review (I copied Laura).
3) Save all evidence in a single folder and keep a running log (example attached: evidence_log_park.xlsx).
4) Schedule the kickoff as a private 1:1; we do not include external counsel in the first conversation.

Attachments: performance_support_template_v1.docx; evidence_log_park.xlsx; manager_checklist.pdf

Two quick HR notes:
- Use neutral language focusing on support and expectations, avoid phrasing that implies pre-judgment ("will be terminated if...").
- Keep conversations brief and fact-oriented; escalate to HR for any mention of misconduct.

I'll leave legal to comment on anything transactional in the template. If you'd like, I can draft the initial goals and the kickoff script and share it back for your edit.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior People Partner
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Support plan for Ethan Park — legal comments

Thanks for the heads up. I reviewed the template and added a few redlines (attached) focused on:
- Notice language: remove phrases that could be construed as a binding ultimatum; we recommend "areas for improvement and expectations to be met within X days".
- Documentation: preserve all Jira tickets and Slack threads relevant to incidents; we should snapshot critical messages where possible.
- Sign-off workflow: manager + HR sign-off before sending to employee; Legal to be looped only if the employee contests or if there's potential for claims.

I'd also flag the following operational items:
1) Do not include speculative dates for termination in the template — keep the timeline for improvement and next-evaluation date.
2) If you plan to require additional training/certifications, make sure we document access and any company-provided resources.

I attached a redlined copy (performance_support_template_v1_LB.docx). Happy to jump on a 20-min call if you want to go line-by-line.

Warmly,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Employment Law
Redwood Inference
Attachment: performance_support_template_v1_LB.docx (redlines)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 12:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Support plan for Ethan Park — need template + legal sign-off

Thanks both — Laura's redlines look sensible. A couple of follow-ups from my side:
- Can you propose 3 concrete, measurable goals for a 60-day window (delivery cadence, code review quality metric, on-call handoff checklist success rate)? I can tailor them but would value a manager-friendly starting point.
- Manager script: would like two versions — (a) supportive script for kickoff, (b) firmer script if there's disengagement at follow-ups.
- If HR signs off, can we have DocuSign/acknowledgment workflow so we record the employee's receipt?

Also: If the employee refuses to sign or declines the meeting, what immediate next step do you recommend? (I want to avoid ad-hoc reactions).

I can be available Friday morning for the call.

-Karthik

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Support plan for Ethan Park — next steps and packet

Karthik —

I've updated the packet with Laura's redlines and filled in a manager-first set of goals below. I've attached the finalized packet and manager checklist; the DocuSign envelope will be generated once you confirm the final language.

Recommended 60-day measurable goals (suggested baseline):
- Delivery cadence: complete 4 feature tickets of the agreed scope with <= 10% scope creep (tracked by linked Jira tickets).
- Code review quality: reduce reviewer rework rate to <15% (we'll use the pull request revert/bug-backlog metric over the 60-day window).
- On-call handoffs: achieve successful handoff checklist in 8 of 8 scheduled rotations; failures to follow checklist require immediate written remediation steps.

Manager scripts enclosed: kickoff (support-focused, 10–15 min), follow-up (30 min weekly checkpoint template), and escalation language for no-shows. For refusal/no-show: do not escalate publicly; document attempt(s) to meet and proceed with follow-up via email giving one more documented opportunity. If the employee still refuses, escalate to HR for next-step recommendations (legal will advise on any involuntary steps).

Attachments: performance_support_template_v1.docx (final), manager_checklist.pdf, evidence_log_park.xlsx
Related link: https://app.docusign.com/sign/abc123xyz

I will:
- Draft the DocuSign acknowledgment for receipt and your manager checklist signature once you reply with any edits.
- Reserve Friday 10:00–10:30 AM for a quick prep call; invite sent pending your confirmation.

Thanks — we will keep this confined to the small group.

-Jasmine Liu
Senior People Partner
Redwood Inference
